description: Local document conversion service: PDF/Office/images/CSV -> markdown, HTML, text, structured JSON, layout-JSON, or CSV/tables. OCR on your GPU-queued Studio/Ollama (external) or an in-pod Ollama (local).
fullDescription:
## OVERVIEW ##
Docling is a document CONVERSION service. It turns PDFs, Office files, images and CSV into markdown, HTML, plain text, structured JSON, layout JSON, or CSV/HTML tables. Text documents parse on the CPU; OCR/vision recognition runs on a pluggable LLM backend (your GPU-queued ComfyUI Studio/Ollama, or an in-pod Ollama). Nothing leaves the machine.

## OUTPUT FORMATS (POST /v1/convert, field 'format') ##
- markdown / html / text - full-document transcription
- json - structured field extraction; pass an optional JSON 'schema' to shape it
- layout-json - elements with bbox + category + text
- csv / tables - tables extracted (text PDFs use deterministic table geometry, no LLM; scanned docs use the element pipeline)

## RECOGNIZERS (POST /v1/convert, field 'recognizer') ##
- dots (default) - end-to-end: the whole page becomes the output in one call. Best all-round.
- paddle-vl - element pipeline: a CPU layout model detects regions, each region is OCR'd, then reassembled (structured OTSL tables). Requires layout.enabled.

## ENDPOINTS ##
- POST /v1/convert  {sources:[{filename, base64_string}], format, recognizer?, schema?, options?} -> {document:{content}, ...}
- POST /v1/layout   {filename, base64_string} -> {boxes:[{bbox, category, score}]} (CPU layout)
- POST /v1/convert/source  back-compat; returns markdown as document.md_content
- POST /render      returns page images (base64 PNG) for scanned docs
- GET  /health      status + active backend + supported formats

## CONFIGURATION (config.json) ##
All behavior - backend, recognizers, extractor, CPU layout model, prompts, formats, thresholds - lives in config.json, mounted at /wrapper/config.json (the docling-wrapper ConfigMap). Edit that ConfigMap and 'kubectl rollout restart deploy/docling' to change prompts or models. NO secrets are stored there.

## LLM BACKEND: EXTERNAL vs LOCAL (chart value backend.mode) ##
EXTERNAL (default): recognition runs on your ComfyUI Studio LLM API (auto: http://comfyuistudio.<namespace>:3002/api/llm/v1), which owns the single-GPU queue. The docling pod stays CPU-only. Needs the API-key Secret (below). The model ids named in config.json (hf.co/...) must already exist on that Ollama.

LOCAL (standalone / independent install): an in-pod Ollama sidecar serves the models on localhost:11434 (NOT exposed outside the pod). The pod then requires a GPU (runtimeClassName nvidia is added automatically). Models are SEEDED on first start: HuggingFace's own client downloads each GGUF (model + mmproj) and 'ollama create' registers it - because 'ollama pull hf.co/...' fails on HF's cross-host xet CDN ('blocked redirect to a different host'). Configure models in backend.localModels as {name, repo}; 'name' must match the recognizer/extractor 'local_model' in config.json, and 'repo' is an HF GGUF repo containing a model *.gguf plus an *mmproj*.gguf. The default seeds dots-ocr (the default recognizer); add olmocr-2 and paddleocr-vl repos to enable format=json and recognizer=paddle-vl in local mode.

TO SWITCH: set backend.mode=local (and provide backend.localModels) at install/upgrade. Everything else - the wrapper, endpoints, config.json - is identical; only where the LLM runs changes.

## CPU LAYOUT (chart value layout.enabled, default true) ##
When enabled, an init container installs paddlepaddle+paddleocr (CPU, from PyPI) into the cache for the PP-DocLayoutV3 layout model. It is used ONLY by recognizer=paddle-vl and the csv/tables/layout formats. The default recognizer (dots) needs none of it - set layout.enabled=false for the leanest, fully CPU pod.

## API KEY (external mode) ##
The API key is read at runtime from a Kubernetes Secret (default name 'docling-vlm', key 'STUDIO_API_KEY') and is never stored in the package. The CPU/text paths work without it.
1. In ComfyUI Studio -> Settings -> API keys, create a key with the 'chat:write' scope.
2. kubectl -n <namespace> create secret generic docling-vlm --from-literal=STUDIO_API_KEY='sk_...'
3. kubectl -n <namespace> rollout restart deploy/docling

upgradeDescription:
1.2.3 - Document conversion service: pluggable LLM backend (external Studio/Ollama or in-pod local Ollama), selectable recognizer (dots end-to-end / paddle-vl element pipeline), and multi-format /v1/convert (markdown, html, text, json, layout-json, csv, tables). All behavior in config.json. Local mode seeds Ollama via HuggingFace download + 'ollama create' (works around the hf.co xet redirect). CPU layout (PP-DocLayoutV3) gated by layout.enabled. Text-PDF tables -> CSV via deterministic geometry. Back-compat /v1/convert/source retained.
1.1.3 — Add a /render endpoint (page images) enabling Studio's fast path: a scanned PDF sent to a vision model is answered from page images in one call, skipping OCR. 1.1.2 — Scanned pages are transcribed by calling the vision model directly (render + OpenAI request) instead of docling's VLM pipeline, avoiding a docling markdown-reassembly crash; output code-fence stripping. 1.1.1 — Auto-download CPU-pipeline models via an init container. 1.1.0 — Scanned PDFs/images parse on-GPU via an Ollama vision model (through the Studio LLM API queue); text documents use the fast CPU pipeline. Add a Studio API key as the 'docling-vlm' Secret to enable the scanned-doc path.
